mentl/5334230:
C1 (W2) · `><` branching affine ledger.
Consume effect extended with branch_enter / branch_divider /
branch_exit. affine_ledger carries a `branches` stack of
(base, deltas) frames; branch_enter snapshots `used` as base;
branch_divider captures the just-finished branch's delta (names
consumed since base) and resets `used` to base so the next branch
sees the original scope; branch_exit captures the last delta,
pairwise-checks all deltas for collisions (each overlap fires
E_OwnershipViolation at the branching span), and merges deltas
into `used` as base ∪ ⋃ deltas. Stack shape supports nested
branches. Substrate cost: O(branches²) comparisons per frame —
tolerable because branches are source-level parallel verbs
(typically 2-3).

C2 (W3) · `<|` full branch walk.
infer_diverge is a dedicated helper. Input (left) is inferred
once — its consumes happen in the outer scope. The branch tuple
(MakeTupleExpr on the right) runs under a branching ledger so any
two branches that consume the same outer-scope own collide.
Single-branch <| falls through to plain infer_expr(right) — no
ledger cost for the degenerate case. Result type is TTuple of each
branch's inferred return type.

C3 (I11) · newline-sensitive `~>`.
PipeKind splits: PTeeBlock (newline-before-~>) and PTeeInline
(no-newline). Parser carries the distinction via skip_ws_tracked
(returns whether any newline was seen) and effective_prec (block
form lowers to precedence 1, so it binds looser than every other
pipe — capturing the whole preceding chain as body; inline form
keeps the base precedence of 10). Inference and lowering treat
both identically — the parser has already built the correct tree
shape.

C4 (I14 + I16) · handler-install subsumption + handler_stack.
InferCtx handler extends with handler_stack state + inf_push_handler
/ inf_pop_handler / inf_handler_stack ops. HandleExpr pushes
handler_stack_tag(handled_names), pops on exit; PTeeBlock/PTeeInline
push "pipe_tee" (the concrete handler-value identity awaits W4

perennials/536edd0:
The text export was the paper way out: readable forever, and lossy. It
carried her kept list and her notes and dropped her yards, her spots, her
bloom dates, her zone and every value she fills in herself, and it could
not be read back at all. A backup you cannot restore is a printout.

Two files go out now. The .json round-trips all eight stores including her
photos, and is the one the app can read; the .txt still outlives the app,
because plain text needs no parser and no version. Photos ride inside the
JSON as data URLs: the alternatives are a zip, which no browser primitive
builds, or a second file she has to keep next to the first, and losing it
is the whole failure mode.

It lives on Field notes rather than Kept because it stopped being about the
kept list. A control that saves seven other things does not belong in the
corner of one of them.

Restore defaults to merge, newest wins. The realistic restore is her second
device: notes here, notes there, and a restore that wipes the phone she is
holding is data loss wearing a feature's clothes. Every store has a natural
identity, so the union is well defined. Replace stays, named for what it
does. A bloom mark merges on (plant, day), because two phones marking the
same plant on the same day is one observation.

The merge is the only part of this that can destroy work she cannot get
back, so it is a pure function with five rules pinned in rules.test.ts
rather than a closure inside an async that touches four kinds of storage.

Every write goes through the store that owns the key, never through
localStorage. createLocalStore.write already refreshes the cache and pokes
its subscribers, so a restore lands live: the kept list, the notes, the
calendar, the yards, the theme and the home-zone sort all re-render on the
spot, and nothing reloads. Writing the keys raw left sixteen
useSyncExternalStore readers on a stale cache, and a reload was the only
thing that could dig them out; that was a bandage over a wound this made.
